clues: This city is in Chad. It leads the Salamat region as its capital, with towns and small villages spread all round it.
The dry season lasts for seven long months each year. When it bites, folks dig deep in the dry river bed for water.
In 1971, French troops built up the sand airport so planes could fly in supplies for the war. Those troops were the French Foreign Legion.
Tell a friend this wild fact: back then, the only real way in or out of this town was by plane. Its sand airport was the town's lifeline.
Zakouma National Park gives it away. This park sits in the wide lands this Chad town leads as its capital.
